program_meta.faculty_directory_url: https://www.kth.se/directory/j/jrr (RPL - Robotics, Perception & Learning full staff directory, the most relevant division for interests A-D); https://www.kth.se/rpl (RPL research-area overview); https://www.kth.se/en/eecs (EECS school top level, for other ML-relevant groups e.g. Theoretical Computer Science, Machine Learning group under Software and Computer Systems)
program_meta.advisor_model: MSc admission is to the PROGRAMME (Machine Learning), not to an individual professor or lab - there is no PhD-style advisor-matching at the application stage. Selection is a numeric merit score (scale 1-75) based on stated criteria (see notes), with no faculty-level interview or advisor assignment.
program_meta.ms_research_access: Yes, via the mandatory final-semester degree project (thesis), which by design 'involves participating in advanced research or design projects in an academic or industrial environment, in Sweden or abroad' (programme page). Students choose/arrange a specific supervisor and project themselves in their final year - i.e. lab access happens organically at the end of Year 1/start of Year 2, not at admission. There is no formal 'apply to join lab X' step in the MSc application itself; a prospective-student email to a specific RPL professor ahead of time is a strategy to pre-arrange a thesis project but is NOT part of the admissions process and does not influence the 1-75 merit score.
program_meta.notes: Acceptance rate: VERBATIM, 'The acceptance rate for the master's programme in Machine Learning for 2026 was 6%. We admitted 58 students out of the 1019 applicants who met the admission requirements.' Extremely selective - among the lowest-acceptance KTH master's programmes. Selection criteria, VERBATIM: '1. Grades from previous study and particularly in subjects relevant to the programme. 2. Motivation for studies (awards, prizes, publications and letters of motivation). 3. Prior education.' Prior education is also weighted by 'university ranking' for international applicants. Specific prerequisite courses required, VERBATIM: 'A Bachelor's degree...with at least one level in mathematics and computer science that corresponds to the courses below at KTH: SF1624 Algebra and Geometry; SF1625 Calculus in One Variable; SF1626 Calculus in Several Variables; SF1920 Probability Theory and Statistics; DD1337 Programming; DD1338 Algorithms and Data Structures.' A separate mandatory 'Summary sheet' must be submitted via a Google-Forms-style KTH survey link (survey.kth.se/tmaim26 for the 2026-cycle; a new link will be issued for the 2027 cycle) - VERBATIM: 'If you do not submit a complete summary sheet, it will negatively affect your evaluation score. Fill out all required information before submitting the form.' This is a required, easy-to-miss administrative step separate from the universityadmissions.se upload. GAPS: universityadmissions.se's own generic deadline and English-test-waiver pages returned 404/not-found during this pass and were not independently cross-checked against the KTH-stated 15 Jan/1 Feb dates - low residual risk, but re-verify closer to the cycle. Full ML-specific tuition figure and the exact TOEFL iBT-equivalent of the stated 'TOEFL score of 4.5' were not resolved and should be re-checked.

faculty.department: Division of Robotics, Perception and Learning (RPL), School of EECS
faculty.lab: Not separately named on her KTH profile; group/people list at kth.se/profile/hedvig/page/people
faculty.research_areas: Computer vision / generative modelling of humans and animals, organized under three themes: AI for Performing Arts, AI for Healthcare, AI for Animal Science. Recent work includes generative-model evaluation, gesture/motion recognition, and facial expression reconstruction with direct supervision.
faculty.why_match: Her 2026 preprint 'RA-ClipScore: Making generative model evaluation more interpretable' (arXiv:2608.12088, 2026) attacks exactly the problem Akshat solved by hand in A-PDF - that standard automatic scores for generative-model output (there, CLIPScore; for Akshat, the GAN discriminator) can be uninterpretable or misleading, and that a more principled, human-interpretable post-hoc quality signal is needed before trusting synthetic samples. Akshat's A-PDF scores cWGAN-GP-generated segmentation masks against the class-proportion distribution of real masks rather than trusting the discriminator, lifting the student model 4% Dice - the same 'don't trust the generator's own score, build an external interpretable one' move Kjellström is making for generative evaluation broadly.
faculty.key_paper_1: RA-ClipScore: Making generative model evaluation more interpretable. arXiv:2608.12088, 2026.
faculty.key_paper_2: FIELDS: Face reconstruction with accurate inference of expression using learning with direct supervision. arXiv:2511.21245v3, 2026.
faculty.taking_students: Not stated on the profile page read in this pass - no explicit prospective-student notice. She is Vice-Director-level engaged with the ML programme (teaches DD2301, examines multiple DAxxxX/EAxxxX degree-project courses including the ML-specialization one, DA233X) and is an active Editor-in-Chief of CVIU and CVPR 2025 Program Chair, indicating an active, current group. Re-check her people page directly for open positions before contacting.
faculty.contact_policy: Not stated - no emailing instructions found on her KTH profile.
faculty.email_angle: Your RA-ClipScore work argues that generative-model evaluation needs an interpretable, non-discriminator signal; I built a small version of that idea for segmentation masks - scoring cWGAN-GP outputs against the class-proportion distribution of real masks rather than trusting the discriminator - and would like to understand what makes such a filter generalize.
faculty.notes: Domain mismatch to flag honestly: her current output (performing arts, animal science, gesture recognition, faces) is far from medical imaging; the connection is purely methodological (interpretable post-hoc generative quality scoring), not domain-matched. She is ELLIS Unit Sweden affiliated and a KTH ML programme instructor, so naming her in the SOP has programme-relevance value even if she is not the primary target.

faculty.research_areas: Deep learning (generative and discriminative), understanding model mechanisms, reasoning, inductive biases, uncertainty estimation and knowledge transfer, applied mainly to computer vision with interdisciplinary interest in life science and physics. Teaches Deep Generative Models and Synthesis (DD2601) and Deep Learning, Advanced Course (DD2412/DD2610).
faculty.why_match: His stated research thrust - VERBATIM from his KTH About Me - is 'advancing them [deep nets] particularly through equipping them with reasoning, inductive biases, uncertainty estimation and knowledge transfer,' applied to computer vision with explicit interest in 'life science.' That is close to a one-line summary of Akshat's whole portfolio: DDPM pretraining as a form of knowledge transfer (liver Dice 0.75->0.93, kidney frozen-encoder failure - a negative result about which inductive bias transfers and which does not), MC-dropout uncertainty for pseudo-label filtering, and HiME's hierarchy constraint as an inductive bias built into the architecture. His explicit life-science interest is also the best-verified bridge at KTH RPL to Akshat's medical-imaging work.
